## Requirement acceptance and evidence

| Requirement | Acceptance criteria | Status | Evidence | Open finding |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `REQ-001` | Root project guidance and ontology discovery identify the same Curator process, its configured project root and its supported owner routes; a bounded representative maintenance operation reaches the applicable current owner and produces attributable evidence under that owner's rules., File presence, policy validity or ontology label discovery alone cannot establish completion of root process integration. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-002` | Ontology queries can identify what each represented function does, its inputs and outputs, responsible owner, affected scope and prerequisites, with references to the installed governing source; unsupported operations are not presented as available., The representation distinguishes Curator coordination from the canonical Task, memory, ontology and integration operations it coordinates. A name-only Curator capability entry fails acceptance. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-003` | Bounded capability, relationship and current-authority queries answer what Curator maintains, which owner controls a selected action, what triggers evaluation, and which source governs the result; outputs identify the exact source/version context and preserve ambiguity, missing-source and stale-source diagnostics., Capability declaration, installation, configuration, authorization, compatibility, runtime observation, pending work and completed owner outcomes remain distinguishable. A historical ontology statement or memory record cannot replace a current owner/authority check., Relevant generated ontology indexes, wiki and memory links remain consistent with the selected canonical Curator knowledge through their existing explicit maintenance operations; retrieval itself performs no repair or canonical write. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-004` | The reviewed source-to-Template inventory accounts for the functional ontology content, bindings or specialization inputs, owner interfaces and project-session assets required by REQ-002 and REQ-003; source and Template checks detect omitted or incompatible integration resources., The Template retains neutral project identity, unbound publication authority and disabled session operation. It contains no root-specific live owner, maintenance backlog, learned record, project-instance claim or runtime evidence, while still supplying the complete reusable integration., Reusable changes originate in their owning source collections and reach only the registered Template through its checked update pipeline; root adoption and selected destination adoption remain distinct operations. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-005` | A representative new project created from the reviewed Template has destination-consistent Curator and ontology identity, source bindings, local owner routes and the discoverable functions/relationships in REQ-002 and REQ-003, without a separate manual ontology-integration step., The resulting project has session maintenance enabled by the selected installation policy, subject to an explicit destination opt-out; its neutral runtime and service choices are preserved. Setup evidence distinguishes static readiness from a separately observed live session. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-006` | Representative first preparation of an existing project and of an unspecialized Template copy yields the functional project and ontology integration required by REQ-002 and REQ-003, specialized to that destination, without a further manual ontology step., Existing customizations and opt-outs remain intact. When preserved content prevents compatible integration, the workflow identifies the exact blocked capability and required selected reconciliation instead of reporting healthy integrated setup. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-007` | Representative prior initialized destinations can receive both parts of the integration through one supported selected workflow, with no separately omitted manual ontology-integration step; unavailable prerequisites or protected conflicts produce exact diagnostics and no false success., Original setup editions, source inventories and receipts remain unchanged historical evidence. New adoption evidence identifies the selected integration edition and current destination state separately, using the existing setup receipt/history mechanism., An ordinary rerun verifies its recorded edition without silently acquiring the new integration. Unselected registered projects remain untouched; an existing disabled setting remains disabled. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-008` | Before/after comparison accounts for every intended integration addition or selected change and proves preservation of unrelated project-owned material. Compatible pre-existing knowledge remains usable without wholesale graph or package replacement., Customized, incompatible, partial or concurrently changed inputs produce attributable conflict or partial-operation evidence. Exact unchanged reruns resume or verify without duplicate capabilities, bindings or registrations; changed sources or destination edits cannot be replayed as an earlier approved operation., Existing session-disabled, capture-off and disabled publication choices survive preparation, adoption and reruns. No existing-project or ontology overwrite authority is inferred from file equality, directory location or registry membership. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-009` | A representative enabled session records changed-input catch-up and routes eligible work through the applicable current owner within the configured bounds. Collection, admission, dispatch and completed owner outcomes are reported separately; unavailable owners or exhausted budgets retain pending work., Session checks and ontology queries do not create an unattended AI service, start a scheduler, invent a native actor, create a second canonical writer or acquire publication authority. Ontology discovery and saved memory do not themselves trigger canonical ontology updates., Existing disabled session choices remain effective, and operation-specific authority, exact source checks and current Task lifecycle gates remain enforced for manual and session-origin work. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-010` | Each still-relevant reported obligation is traced to its current delivery and owning workflow, then either completed with an attributable canonical owner receipt or retained with a specific blocker, owner and next eligible action. Already completed or superseded items retain their supporting history., A delivery is consumed only after its completed owner outcome. Metadata row counts and partial path pages are not represented as failure counts, full source validation or completed maintenance; source drift requires a fresh observation. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-011` | The investigation identifies the exact current staged artifact, related transaction evidence, canonical Task revision/status and known write-owning assignments. It records whether the artifact is recoverable, already represented or requires a specific owner action without inferring safety from age, cancellation or roster absence alone., Any authorized disposition uses the supported exact Task operation, preserves response history and unrelated work, and is followed by rereading the canonical Task state and running validation. If the evidence or authority is insufficient, the artifact remains preserved with a precise blocker; no Task is falsely completed or silently reopened. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-012` | A separately authorized on-demand verification opens the selected local workbench and exercises a representative read/navigation flow against the intended root. It records the observed result and safe lifecycle disposition while protecting the private session token., Health evidence distinguishes not running, not assessed, observed operational and failed behavior. An absent endpoint alone is not classified as a failed service, and read/navigation evidence does not imply guarded writes or canonical publication passed. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-013` | Fresh applicable health checks and a bounded actual memory retrieval demonstrate no integration regression against the previously working behavior, including canonical validity, relevant source freshness, projections and memory links., Existing authored facts, accepted memory records, capture settings and locked imports retain their meaning and provenance. Unrelated backends, schemas, runtimes and publication grants are not changed to make the integration appear healthy. | `active` | 0 | None |
| `REQ-014` | Evidence demonstrates functional ontology queries and coherent project wiring in the root and representative new, first-prepared and prior-initialized destinations; Template evidence proves neutral reusable completeness. Each route rejects file-install-only or missing-ontology success., The report separates static contract checks, fixture checks, actual owner execution, browser observation and end-to-end setup behavior. It identifies any remaining blocker or unexercised behavior without describing the associated requirement as satisfied., Current hashes, source/destination scope, receipts and final state support the reported result. The dated health report remains preserved, and no fixture or configured flag is substituted for a live observation. | `active` | 0 | None |
